sections.content: How many people stayed in Goldthorpe after gaining qualifications?

Goldthorpe is a small town in Yorkshire and The Humber. Goldthorpe does not have its own university.

Goldthorpe has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Goldthorpe ended up with:

  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

In Goldthorpe, 340 state school pupils sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 2011 school years.

Of these, 45 (13%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as definied by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 90 (26%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Goldthorpe to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Goldthorpe's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Goldthorpe in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there in 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, all affected students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

In 2018 to 2019, 57% of qualified non-graduates living in Goldthorpe had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 105 qualified non-graduates from our cohort living in Goldthorpe, compared with the 90 qualified non-graduates who sat their GCSEs there.

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, 43% of qualified non-graduates in Goldthorpe had sat their GCSEs there, while 57% had moved there from elsewhere.
